sn12.25:1.2: Now the venerable Bhūmija, arising at eventide from solitary meditation, came into the presence of the venerable Sāriputta, and exchanging greetings with him and compliments of friendship and courtesy sat down at one side,
sn12.25:1.3: and so seated said thus to him:—
sn12.25:2.1: “There are, friend Sāriputta, certain recluses and brahmins, believers in karma, who declare that happiness and ill have been made by one's self;
sn12.25:2.2: certain others who say that happiness and ill have been made by another;
sn12.25:2.3: certain others who say both cases are true;
sn12.25:2.4: certain others who say that neither case is true, but that happiness and ill arise by chance.
sn12.25:2.5: Herein, friend Sāriputta, the Exalted One what has he to tell us?
sn12.25:2.6: And how, if we were answering, should we be repeating his views correctly and not be misrepresenting him, nor rendering ourselves open to blame?”
sn12.25:3.1: “The Exalted One has said, friend, that happiness and ill come to pass through a cause,
sn12.25:4.1: In the case of those recluses and brahmins who believe in karma, however they say that happiness and ill have been made, it was because of contact that they came to pass.
sn12.25:5.1: In no one of those four views is it possible to show that those recluses and brahmins will experience happiness or ill without contact.”
sn12.25:6.2: and he went into the presence of the Exalted One
sn12.25:7.1: And the Exalted One praised Sāriputta through him and confirmed all that he had said and said yet further:—
sn12.25:10.1: “Where there have been deeds, Ānanda, personal happiness and suffering arise in consequence of the will there was in the deeds.
sn12.25:10.2: Where there has been speech—where there has been thought, personal happiness and suffering arise in consequence of the will there was in the speech—in the thought.
sn12.25:11.1: Either we of ourselves, Ānanda, plan those planned deeds conditioned by ignorance, whence so caused arises personal happiness and suffering.
sn12.25:11.2: or others plan those planned deeds that we do conditioned by ignorance, whence so conditioned arises personal happiness and suffering.
sn12.25:12.1: Thence both ways arises personal happiness and suffering. So also is it where there has been speech,
sn12.25:13.1: Either we plan, speaking, thinking deliberately
sn12.25:13.2: or others plan, so that we speak, think unwittingly.
sn12.25:13.4: Thence arises personal happiness and suffering.
sn12.25:14.1: In these six cases ignorance is followed after.
sn12.25:14.2: But from the utter fading away and cessation of ignorance, Ānanda, those deeds are not, whence so conditioned arises personal happiness and suffering. Neither is that speech, nor that thought.
sn12.25:14.3: As field they are not; as base they are not; as wherewithal they are not; as occasion they are not, that so conditioned there might arise personal happiness and suffering.”
